## America’s Favorite Cities 2008: Where travelers found the best food, fun — and a few flops

The results are in, and the 2008 **America’s Favorite Cities** survey from *Travel + Leisure* offered a snapshot of what travelers loved most — and least — about some of the country’s best-known urban escapes.

The annual reader survey asked travelers to rate major U.S. cities across categories ranging from dining, nightlife and shopping to friendliness, cleanliness, culture, traffic and overall value. The 2008 results showed that some cities kept a tight grip on their reputations, while others surprised voters with big gains — or disappointing finishes.

### The big winners

**New York City** remained the heavyweight in the categories where visitors expect it to dominate: culture, theater, high-end dining, shopping and people-watching. For travelers who want museums by day, restaurants by night and a neighborhood for every mood, New York continued to be the all-purpose urban getaway.

**New Orleans** was another standout, powered by its unmatched personality. The city scored strongly in areas tied to music, nightlife, festivals and distinct local flavor — proof that travelers still see the Crescent City as one of America’s most memorable places to eat, listen and wander.

**Chicago** earned praise for its architecture, skyline, museums and food scene, giving travelers another reason to see it as more than a business-trip destination. Summer remains the ideal time to go: lakefront walks, outdoor dining, baseball and neighborhood festivals are all part of the appeal.

**San Francisco** continued to do well with travelers seeking romance, scenery, restaurants and walkable neighborhoods. From ferry rides and hilltop views to North Beach cafés and the Mission’s dining scene, the city’s compact geography remains one of its biggest assets.

**Charleston** and **Santa Fe** stood out among smaller, atmosphere-rich destinations. Both cities have long appealed to travelers looking for charm, local culture, strong regional cuisine and a slower pace than the country’s biggest metros.

### The cities that struggled

Not every city came out glowing.

Cities known for sprawl and traffic — including **Los Angeles** and **Atlanta** — tended to suffer in categories tied to ease of getting around. Even where visitors praised food, shopping or nightlife, congestion and car dependence dragged down the experience.

Some destinations also had image problems. Cities that travelers associated with poor cleanliness, weak value or less friendly locals found themselves near the bottom in those quality-of-life categories. The survey reinforced a familiar travel truth: a great restaurant scene can help, but it may not overcome bad traffic, high prices or a stressful arrival.

### What changed from 2007

The 2008 survey reflected a broader shift in what travelers were paying attention to. Compared with 2007, voters appeared increasingly interested in the details that make a city feel livable as well as visitable: neighborhood dining, local culture, walkability, parks, public spaces and authenticity.

Food categories also became more nuanced. Instead of simply asking whether a city had “good restaurants,” travelers were weighing cities by specific cravings — fine dining, ethnic food, casual eats, cafés, local specialties and nightlife scenes.

That helped cities with strong neighborhood identities rise in the conversation. Places like Portland, Austin, Seattle, New Orleans and San Francisco benefited from traveler interest in cities that feel distinctive rather than interchangeable.

Meanwhile, traditional glamour still mattered. New York, Las Vegas, Miami and Los Angeles remained powerful draws for shopping, hotels, nightlife and celebrity appeal — even when they didn’t win on ease, value or friendliness.

### Where to go based on your travel style

**For food lovers:**  
Head to New York for range, New Orleans for flavor, San Francisco for restaurants and markets, Chicago for deep-dish and fine dining, and Santa Fe for Southwestern cuisine.

**For nightlife:**  
New Orleans, Las Vegas, Miami, New York and Austin are the obvious contenders. Choose New Orleans for live music, Vegas for spectacle, Miami for late nights and Austin for a more casual, music-first scene.

**For culture:**  
New York, Washington, D.C., Chicago, Boston and San Francisco remain reliable picks for museums, architecture, history and performing arts.

**For romance:**  
San Francisco, Charleston, Santa Fe, Honolulu and New Orleans all make strong cases, depending on whether your idea of romance involves ocean views, old streets, desert sunsets or jazz after dark.

**For a long weekend:**  
Charleston, New Orleans, Santa Fe, Portland and Nashville are especially good choices. Each offers a concentrated dose of food, music, neighborhoods and atmosphere without requiring a weeklong itinerary.

**For travelers who hate driving:**  
New York, Boston, Chicago, San Francisco and Washington, D.C. are easier bets. If you’re visiting Los Angeles, Atlanta, Phoenix or Dallas, plan around traffic and choose a neighborhood base carefully.

### The takeaway

The 2008 America’s Favorite Cities results suggest that travelers were rewarding cities with personality. Big sights still mattered, but voters also wanted good local food, memorable neighborhoods, music, public spaces and a sense that they were somewhere unique.

In other words: the best cities weren’t just the biggest or flashiest. They were the places that gave visitors a story to bring home.

### Now it’s your turn: vote in the bracket

Think New York is unbeatable? Believe New Orleans has the most soul? Ready to defend Chicago, Charleston, San Francisco, Austin or Seattle?

Cast your vote in the **America’s Favorite Cities bracket game** and help decide which destination deserves the ultimate bragging rights. Pick your favorites, follow the matchups and see whether your city can survive the next round.

## America’s Favorite Cities Rankings: Surprising Results—and Where to Travel Next Based on What You Love

The latest America’s Favorite Cities rankings are full of conversation-starting surprises. Some of the country’s most iconic destinations landed in unexpected spots, including Philadelphia being ranked among the least attractive cities and Los Angeles receiving low marks for friendliness. But as any seasoned traveler knows, rankings only tell part of the story.

A city that disappoints one visitor may delight another. The best trip is often less about where a destination lands on a list and more about whether it matches your travel style—food, culture, nightlife, outdoor adventure, romance, family fun, or pure relaxation.

So before you cross any city off your list, consider what you actually want from your next getaway.

### The Big Surprise: Philadelphia’s Low “Attractiveness” Ranking

Philadelphia may have been ranked least attractive in the survey, but that does not mean it lacks appeal. In fact, Philly remains one of America’s most historic, walkable, and culturally rich cities.

Travelers who love history can visit Independence Hall, the Liberty Bell, and Elfreth’s Alley, one of the oldest residential streets in the country. Art lovers can spend hours at the Philadelphia Museum of Art, the Barnes Foundation, and the city’s many murals. And food-focused travelers will find far more than cheesesteaks, from Reading Terminal Market to acclaimed restaurants in Fishtown and Center City.

**Best for:** history lovers, food travelers, museum-goers, weekend city breaks  
**Don’t miss:** Reading Terminal Market, Old City, Philadelphia Museum of Art, Rittenhouse Square

### Los Angeles Ranked Least Friendly—But Still Hard to Resist

Los Angeles may have scored low for friendliness, but the city’s appeal has never depended on small-town charm. L.A. is sprawling, stylish, creative, and endlessly varied. It is a destination where visitors can build completely different vacations in the same city.

Beach lovers can stay in Santa Monica or Venice. Film fans can explore Hollywood, studio tours, and classic movie locations. Food lovers can chase tacos, Korean barbecue, sushi, and celebrity-chef restaurants. Outdoor travelers can hike Runyon Canyon, Griffith Park, or the trails above Malibu.

L.A. may not always feel instantly welcoming, but for travelers who arrive with a plan, it can be one of the most rewarding cities in the country.

**Best for:** beach escapes, entertainment, food, nightlife, shopping  
**Don’t miss:** Griffith Observatory, Getty Center, Santa Monica, Malibu, Koreatown

---

## Where to Go Based on Your Travel Personality

### For Food Lovers: New Orleans, Chicago, and San Francisco

If your ideal itinerary revolves around where to eat next, head to a city with a distinct culinary identity.

**New Orleans** is perfect for travelers who want food with music, history, and atmosphere. Think gumbo, po’boys, beignets, and long dinners in the French Quarter or Garden District.

**Chicago** delivers deep-dish pizza, Michelin-starred dining, neighborhood taverns, and one of the country’s most exciting restaurant scenes.

**San Francisco** remains a classic for seafood, sourdough, farmers markets, Chinatown dining, and nearby wine country excursions.

### For Romance: Charleston, Savannah, and Santa Barbara

Some cities seem designed for slow walks, candlelit dinners, and boutique hotels.

**Charleston** offers cobblestone streets, pastel homes, waterfront views, and refined Southern cuisine.

**Savannah** is atmospheric and dreamy, with moss-draped squares, historic inns, and a relaxed pace.

**Santa Barbara** combines beaches, Spanish-style architecture, wine tasting, and luxury resorts—ideal for a coastal couples’ escape.

### For Families: Orlando, San Diego, and Washington, D.C.

Family travel works best when a destination has plenty to do and easy ways to keep everyone entertained.

**Orlando** remains the obvious choice for theme parks, resorts, and kid-friendly attractions.

**San Diego** offers beaches, the San Diego Zoo, Balboa Park, and a relaxed Southern California feel.

**Washington, D.C.** is a strong pick for families who want museums, monuments, and educational attractions—many of them free.

### For Culture Seekers: New York City, Santa Fe, and Boston

If you travel for museums, architecture, theater, and local identity, these cities should be high on your list.

**New York City** is unmatched for Broadway, galleries, restaurants, shopping, and neighborhoods that feel like worlds of their own.

**Santa Fe** is ideal for art lovers, with Pueblo-style architecture, galleries, Native American culture, and a dramatic desert setting.

**Boston** blends American history, university energy, museums, and walkable neighborhoods.

### For Outdoor Adventure: Denver, Seattle, and Honolulu

Travelers who prefer trails, water, mountains, and fresh air should look west—or across the Pacific.

**Denver** is a gateway to the Rockies, with hiking, skiing, breweries, and an outdoorsy urban culture.

**Seattle** combines city life with access to mountains, islands, forests, and Puget Sound.

**Honolulu** offers beaches, surfing, hiking, volcanic landscapes, and a blend of urban and island experiences.

### For Nightlife: Las Vegas, Miami, and Nashville

If your vacation begins after sunset, choose a city built for entertainment.

**Las Vegas** is still the ultimate nightlife destination, with clubs, casinos, shows, restaurants, and resort pools.

**Miami** offers beach clubs, Latin music, rooftop bars, and late-night energy.

**Nashville** is ideal for live music lovers, from honky-tonks on Broadway to intimate songwriter venues.

### For a Relaxing Escape: Sedona, Palm Springs, and Key West

Not every trip needs a packed itinerary.

**Sedona** is known for red-rock views, spas, hiking, and a peaceful desert atmosphere.

**Palm Springs** delivers poolside relaxation, midcentury style, mountain views, and easy access to Joshua Tree.

**Key West** is laid-back, sunny, and quirky, with pastel streets, sunset celebrations, and island time built into the experience.

---

## Why Rankings Should Inspire—not Decide—Your Trip

The most interesting thing about city rankings is not who wins or loses. It is what they reveal about how differently travelers experience the same place.

Philadelphia may not top every beauty list, but it offers depth, history, and one of the best food scenes in the country. Los Angeles may not feel warm and fuzzy to every visitor, but it delivers beaches, culture, glamour, and global cuisine on a massive scale.

The takeaway: use rankings as a starting point, not a final verdict. The “best” city is the one that fits the vacation you actually want.

Whether you are planning a romantic weekend, a family getaway, a food-focused city break, or an outdoor adventure, America’s cities offer plenty of reasons to book the next trip—even when the rankings come with a few surprises.

# America’s Favorite Cities: Travelers Crown Their Top Urban Escapes

**By Travel News Service**

From food-forward weekends and music-filled nights to waterfront strolls and museum-hopping afternoons, America’s favorite cities continue to shift as travelers seek experiences that feel both iconic and personal. This year’s standout destinations reflect a familiar mix of big-city energy, regional character, and vacation-ready neighborhoods where visitors can arrive, wander, and feel instantly immersed.

While longtime favorites remain strong, several cities are gaining attention for their revitalized downtowns, expanding culinary scenes, outdoor access, and year-round cultural calendars.

## Notable Changes: What’s Moving on the City Map

A few trends are shaping how travelers are choosing their favorite U.S. cities right now:

### Smaller Big Cities Are Rising  
Travelers are showing growing affection for cities that offer major experiences without overwhelming scale. Places with walkable districts, standout restaurants, local music, and easy weekend itineraries are increasingly popular.

### Food Is Driving More Trips  
Dining has moved from “nice bonus” to primary reason to visit. Cities known for regional cuisine, chef-led neighborhoods, food halls, farmers markets, and late-night bites are seeing renewed interest.

### Outdoor Access Matters  
Urban vacations are no longer just about buildings, museums, and nightlife. Travelers are favoring cities with nearby beaches, rivers, parks, bike paths, mountain views, or desert trails.

### The Classics Still Count  
New York, Chicago, New Orleans, San Francisco, Boston, Washington, D.C., and Las Vegas remain durable favorites thanks to their unmistakable identities. Travelers continue to return for Broadway lights, deep-dish slices, jazz clubs, cable cars, historic landmarks, and high-energy entertainment.

### Neighborhood Travel Is In  
Instead of trying to “do” an entire city, visitors are choosing a few neighborhoods and exploring them deeply. Local cafés, vintage shops, galleries, breweries, bookstores, and street art are becoming the heart of the modern city vacation.

## Vacation Finder: Recommendations by Travel Style

Not sure which American city should top your list? Try matching your travel mood to the destination.

### For Food Lovers  
**New Orleans, Louisiana** — Creole classics, po’boys, beignets, oysters, and music-filled meals make this city a perennial favorite.  
**Chicago, Illinois** — Beyond deep-dish pizza, Chicago delivers serious fine dining, neighborhood food tours, and global cuisine.  
**Austin, Texas** — Barbecue, breakfast tacos, food trucks, and live music create a vacation rhythm all its own.

### For Culture Seekers  
**Washington, D.C.** — Museums, monuments, historic neighborhoods, and an expanding restaurant scene make it ideal for curious travelers.  
**New York City, New York** — Theater, galleries, fashion, architecture, and round-the-clock energy keep the city at the center of American travel.  
**Santa Fe, New Mexico** — Art markets, adobe architecture, Southwestern cuisine, and desert landscapes offer a distinctive cultural escape.

### For Outdoor Urban Adventures  
**Seattle, Washington** — Coffee, markets, ferries, mountains, and water views make it a favorite for city-and-nature trips.  
**Denver, Colorado** — A lively downtown, brewery scene, and easy access to the Rockies appeal to active travelers.  
**San Diego, California** — Beaches, parks, tacos, and sunny weather create a relaxed coastal city break.

### For Music and Nightlife  
**Nashville, Tennessee** — Honky-tonks, songwriter rounds, hot chicken, and neighborhood stages keep the beat going.  
**New Orleans, Louisiana** — Jazz, brass bands, blues, and late-night clubs make music part of daily life.  
**Las Vegas, Nevada** — Major residencies, casinos, restaurants, and spectacle-packed entertainment remain the draw.

### For Family-Friendly City Trips  
**Orlando, Florida** — Theme parks lead the way, but dining, resorts, and nearby nature add range.  
**San Diego, California** — Beaches, the zoo, museums, and outdoor activities make it easy for all ages.  
**Boston, Massachusetts** — History, harbor views, parks, and walkable neighborhoods offer an educational but fun getaway.

### For Romantic Weekends  
**Charleston, South Carolina** — Historic streets, refined dining, harbor breezes, and charming inns set the mood.  
**Savannah, Georgia** — Shaded squares, riverfront strolls, and atmospheric architecture make it ideal for slow wandering.  
**San Francisco, California** — Bay views, neighborhoods, restaurants, and classic landmarks still deliver romance with a view.

## What’s YOUR Fave?

Now it’s your turn to join the conversation. Which American city wins your vote?

Is it the city with the best pizza? The best skyline? The friendliest locals? The most unforgettable weekend? The one place you keep returning to—or the city that surprised you most?

Play **“What’s YOUR Fave?”** by naming your favorite U.S. city and the reason it tops your list. Whether your pick is a famous classic, a fast-rising hotspot, or a hometown you think deserves more love, America’s favorite cities are ultimately defined by the travelers who explore them.

## Readers’ Choice: The Best (and Most Debated) U.S. Cities Right Now

Every city has its loyalists—and its skeptics. In our reader-voted travel roundup, a few U.S. destinations rose to the top for doing one thing exceptionally well, while others earned mixed reviews for crowds, costs, or convenience. Here’s where travelers say America shines, and where the experience can be more complicated.

### Best City for Fine Dining: New Orleans, Louisiana  
New Orleans continues to be a reader favorite for meals that feel like occasions. From white-tablecloth Creole classics to neighborhood po’boy counters, oyster bars, and late-night plates after jazz shows, the city’s dining scene is both deeply traditional and constantly inventive. Readers praised its sense of place: you don’t just eat in New Orleans—you taste the city’s history.

**Also loved for:** Live music. Whether it’s brass bands, blues, funk, or jazz spilling out of Frenchmen Street clubs, New Orleans was voted one of the country’s best cities for hearing music that feels alive and unpolished in the best possible way.

### Friendliest City: Charleston, South Carolina  
Charleston scored high for Southern hospitality, walkable historic streets, and an easygoing elegance that makes even a weekend trip feel gracious. Readers called out the warmth of hotel staff, restaurant servers, shopkeepers, and locals who seemed genuinely happy to point visitors toward a favorite beach, bar, or biscuit.

**Why readers return:** The combination of charm, architecture, coastal scenery, and polished-but-relaxed dining makes Charleston feel both refined and welcoming.

### Best City for People-Watching: New York City, New York  
No surprise here: New York remains unmatched for sheer human theater. Readers voted it the best city for people-watching, whether from a café window in SoHo, a bench in Bryant Park, the High Line, the subway, or a late-night slice shop. Fashion, ambition, eccentricity, celebrity sightings, and everyday neighborhood rituals all collide here.

**The downside:** Readers also ranked New York among the most expensive and overwhelming cities, especially for first-time visitors. But for many, that intensity is exactly the point.

### Cleanest/Best Outdoorsy City: Portland, Oregon  
Portland earned strong marks for cleanliness, access to nature, and a lifestyle that makes it easy to get outside. Readers liked the city’s parks, bikeability, nearby hikes, and proximity to waterfalls, forests, mountains, and the Oregon coast. It’s a city where a morning coffee, a trail walk, and a great dinner can all fit into the same day.

**Best for:** Travelers who want urban comforts without giving up green space.

### Best City for Kids: Orlando, Florida  
For families, Orlando remains the heavyweight champion. Readers praised its unmatched concentration of theme parks, kid-friendly resorts, entertainment districts, water parks, and restaurants built with children in mind. It’s not always subtle, but it is incredibly efficient at delivering fun.

**The tradeoff:** Crowds, heat, and costs can add up quickly—especially during school breaks—but for many families, the payoff is worth it.

---

## The Most Divisive Cities

### New York City: Best and Worst, Depending on Your Mood  
New York appeared on both “best” and “worst” lists. Readers loved its energy, dining, museums, theater, shopping, and street life—but criticized its prices, crowds, noise, and pace. It’s a city that rewards stamina.

### Orlando: A Dream for Kids, a Test for Adults  
Families praised Orlando’s kid-centered attractions, but some child-free travelers ranked it lower for traffic, sprawl, and a vacation atmosphere that can feel manufactured. In short: magical for the right trip, exhausting for the wrong one.

### New Orleans: Unforgettable, but Not Always Easy  
Readers adored New Orleans for food and music, yet some noted uneven infrastructure, humidity, and nightlife that can get rowdy. Still, few cities left a stronger impression.

---

## Reader Takeaway

The best U.S. city depends on the trip you want. For music and memorable meals, go to **New Orleans**. For gracious hospitality, choose **Charleston**. For street life and spectacle, it’s **New York**. For cleanliness and easy access to the outdoors, try **Portland**. And for a family vacation built around kids, **Orlando** remains hard to beat.
